questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly, I chose Milan for the social aspect of exchange and to experience the Italian culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I received all necessary information before arrival.
It did arrive pretty late - around a week before moving to Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Honestly, I don't know

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Dorm room housing, sharing a room with another student. The dorm was a bit traumatic, but I met so many great people through the dorm. 
You'll get good lore from living there. Campus Martinitt is kinda iconic in that way.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There was a common kitchen shared with all dorm-residents. You'll have to bring your own kitchen supplies, which then got stolen - again, good lore. 
The kitchen got cleaned everyday in the morning, so it was nice and tidy (in the beginning of the day).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
When paying only 300 euros for accommodation in Milan, you'll also get 300 euros accommodation.
Being overbearing is key(!), but it is definitely worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
If you are unsure whether to live in a dorm or not - do it!
I would recommend.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
A bit difficult. You'll have to figure out the system yourself (mental pain). 
Once you figure it out, it was okay.
You can change courses throughout the entire semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I have no idea

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Some of the courses I wanted to take were not available.
So partly successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
hmmmmm, it will be a bit difficult only because no information is provided.
However, when you figure it out, it will be easy.
So have a breakdown and it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was very uncertain.
There was no study material provided, no exercise classes, no expected learning outcomes.
During the exam season, they did not have previous exam sets to look at.
I was very lost throughout the semester, but the exams were easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I missed UCPH...
Again, there was no study material, exercise classes or really any methods of reading up on the courses by yourself in Milan.
Structured learning does not exist in Milan.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Time Series and Forecasting, Game Theory, Business History and Causal Inference and Policy Evaluation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Time Series and Forecasting - learned useful stuff, most structured class and the teacher was great (can also be transferred as Øko II - big win).
Business History was also very great (took it as 'non-attending').

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I spent a lot more than the presented budget. I travelled to other Italian cities as well as other countries.
Also, a lot of spendings on nights out with friends. Going out became a usual thing even on weekdays.
All worth it though.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cheap spritz (depending on how many you end up buying).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Didn't partake in activities provided by host institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on week trips other Italian cities!
There are many great places close to Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the Erasmus-events in the beginning. There is a lot and you'll quickly run into familiar faces

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The no-punctuality thing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The laid-back life styles.
Both a blessing and a curse.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, meet a lot of people, don't stress over uni.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not have high expectations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The university

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
This review seems kinda negative. It is really not meant to be. 
Going on exchange was such a great experience - you get to experience a new daily day, meet tons of great people, gain so many memories ect.
I loved it so much and I would do it all again!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
